steps.description: The warrior begins in a powerful, low Mandi posture, hands in taut Katakamukha mudra (Vajra-Mushti substitute) held aggressively near the chest.
steps.rasa_expression: Intense, narrow-eyed glare (Dūrpārsvāvalokanam); jaw set and shoulders squared, conveying coiled fury.
steps.teaching_note: The Mandi posture must be deep and held with full tension; the gaze must project beyond the viewer, fixing on the imaginary enemy.

steps.description: A sharp, decisive step forward with the right foot, rising slightly to Araimandi, transitioning the right hand to Pataka and thrusting it diagonally down (suggesting drawing a weapon).
steps.rasa_expression: A flash of fierce anger in the eyes (Roudra Drishthi); quick, visible intake of breath through the nose.
steps.teaching_note: The shift from Mandi to Araimandi must be swift and executed with force; the foot-strike must be loud and commanding.

steps.description: Two powerful, wide steps forward (R-L) using a forceful Chauka gait, hands remaining low in Pataka to emphasize forward aggression.
steps.rasa_expression: A slight tremor (Kampa) in the shoulders and chest to show rising, barely contained rage.
steps.teaching_note: Focus on using the entire body to propel forward; the hips and torso must maintain a strong, forward lean.

steps.description: Stops sharply with the left foot planted, left hand returns to Katakamukha near the chest (restraining movement).
steps.rasa_expression: The lips curl slightly (Oshtha-Bandha) into a snarl; a silent, aggressive exhale.
steps.teaching_note: The stop must be instantaneous and controlled, utilizing muscular tension to immediately halt momentum.

steps.description: The right arm (still Pataka) is brought up and thrust out frontally at shoulder level on the first beat, holding the command (stop/challenge) on the second beat.
steps.rasa_expression: The gaze is held unwaveringly (Sthira Drishthi) and focused directly at the imaginary enemy; a momentary widening of the eyes for impact.
steps.teaching_note: The arm extension must be straight, taut, and forceful; the torso must support the forward thrust, leaning slightly into the action.
